answer.reason: The entity preserving parse mode is part of XMLDocument's supported configuration, but the complete old harness always constructs the document with the true default. This blocker is preexisting on the same obligation.
answer.finite_witness: Input bytes: &. Supported setup: XMLDocument(false), followed by Parse, retains & in the text value. The old harness instead constructs XMLDocument with no arguments.

scope_contract.reason: The entry parses XML through XMLDocument. Entity processing is a constructor setting of that same document, and text parsing reads it.

feasible_trigger.reason: The finite XML input contains a recognized entity. Constructing XMLDocument(false) is supported, and the text parser then selects the leave entities mode; the target's fixed construction blocks that setup.

observable_consequence.reason: No target input can exercise entity preserving parsing: the target always selects the true default, which chooses entity processing for ordinary text. This is lost supported behavior, not an invalid existing assertion.

alternatives_ruled_out.reason: The complete entry has one document construction and one Parse call, with no input controlled configuration or second call sequence. CDATA can retain literal characters, but it uses a separate parsing path and does not exercise ordinary text with processEntities=false.

identity_preserved.reason: Before and after, the same XMLDocument constructor setting controls the same ordinary text parsing choice, and the same old harness fixes that setting to its true default. The changed destructor concerns cleanup of those parsed nodes but does not change this tuple.

citations.dependency_reason: The constructor stores the selected entity processing setting.
Ordinary text parsing chooses the leave entities flags when the setting is false.
The selected text flags differ according to the constructor setting.
When entity processing is selected, reading a recognized amp entity converts it to an ampersand.
CDATA and ordinary text use different branches; only ordinary text selects flags from ProcessEntities().
Before source uses the document setting for ordinary text parsing.
After source uses the same document setting for ordinary text parsing.
The before g0001 destructor deletes parsed child nodes.
The after g0001 destructor changes child node cleanup.
